identity.name: Alpine Eagle
identity.one_liner: The 41mm integrated-bracelet sport watch in Chopard's proprietary Lucent Steel A223 — the steel-sport competitor to the Royal Oak and Nautilus that entered the market in 2019.

narrative.story: The Alpine Eagle (2019) is Chopard's entry into the integrated-bracelet steel-sport category defined by the Royal Oak and the Nautilus. The case material is Lucent Steel A223 — a proprietary Chopard alloy that is harder than conventional stainless steel and has a brighter reflectivity. The Chopard 01.01-C caliber is an in-house automatic with a 60-hour reserve. The textured dial references the iris of an eagle. The Alpine Eagle is the most-cited modern Chopard sport watch and the one a collector cites when they want an integrated-bracelet design that is not from the established Swiss trio.
narrative.collector_notes: Lucent Steel A223 is a Chopard-exclusive alloy, recycled and harder than 316L. The Alpine Eagle line was inspired by the 1980 Chopard St. Moritz (Karl-Friedrich Scheufele's first design).
